title: Design Facebook Status Search
prompt:
Design search over the status posts of a large social network. A user types a few words and gets matching posts from people they are connected to, plus public posts, ordered by relevance and recency. Every result must respect the author's audience settings: nobody may ever see a post they are not allowed to see.

Assume **1 billion daily active users** writing about **300 million posts a day**, and about **100 million searches a day**.
clarify: Whose posts are searchable: friends, friends of friends, public posts, groups?
How soon after posting must a status be searchable (seconds or minutes)?
Is search over text only, or also names, hashtags, locations, media captions?
How are results ranked: recency, social closeness, engagement?
What happens when an author edits, deletes or changes the audience of a post?
Do we need typo tolerance and multiple languages?

reference.requirements:
**Functional**
- Keyword (and phrase) search over posts the searcher is allowed to see
- Ranking by relevance, recency and social closeness; pagination
- New posts become searchable quickly; edits and deletes are reflected

**Non-functional**
- Privacy is a correctness requirement, not a ranking signal: zero leakage, including through result counts and stale indexes
- Search latency p99 < 300 ms; index freshness within seconds to a minute
- Write-heavy index maintenance (thousands of posts/s) with moderate query volume
- Horizontally scalable index that can lose machines without losing data
reference.estimation:
- Posts: 300M/day ≈ **3,500/s** average; ~10K/s at peak
- Raw text: 300M × ~300 B ≈ **90 GB/day**
- Index: ~20 distinct terms per post → 300M × 20 = **6B postings/day**; at ~8 B per posting entry that is ~**48 GB/day**, or ~**17.5 TB/year** before compression (delta-coded postings compress ~3–4×). Keep recent months in memory/SSD, older data on cheaper tiers
- Queries: 100M/day ≈ **1,160/s** average, ~3× at peak; each fans out to every index shard that covers the time range
- Takeaway: indexing writes outnumber queries 3:1, so the system is write-path and fan-out bound
reference.api:
```
GET /v1/search/posts?q=weekend+hike&cursor=&limit=20  → {results:[{post_id, author, snippet, ts}], next_cursor}
```
- Viewer identity comes from the auth token; the client never passes who it is searching as.
- Cursor encodes `(score, post_id)` plus the index snapshot so paging is stable.
- Internal: `index(post_event)` consumed from the post-change stream: create, edit, delete, audience-change.
reference.data:
- **Source of truth:** the posts store (sharded by author) holding text and the audience policy.
- **Inverted index:** `term → sorted posting list of post_ids`, with per-posting metadata (author id, time, audience class). Document ids are time-ordered so recent postings are contiguous and cheap to skip.
- **Forward index / doc store:** `post_id → snippet, author, ts` for rendering.
- **Social graph:** `friends(user) → ids`, used both for ranking and for filtering.
- Index shards are partitioned by **time bucket first, then post_id hash** within a bucket.
reference.design:
```
post write ─▶ posts DB ─▶ change stream ─▶ tokenizer ─▶ indexer ─▶ index shards (RAM+SSD, replicated)

search ─▶ query service (parse, expand) ─▶ scatter to shards ─▶ per-shard top-N (term match ∩ audience)
              ▲ friends(viewer)                          └─▶ merge ─▶ privacy re-check ─▶ rank ─▶ page
```
- **Indexing:** a change event is tokenised and applied to the real-time tier of an index shard within seconds; a periodic merge compacts into immutable segments.
- **Query:** fan out to all shards for the recent time buckets (older buckets only on demand), each returns its top candidates, the coordinator merges and re-ranks.
- **Privacy** is enforced twice: inside the index query and again against the authoritative policy.
reference.deepdives:
- **Privacy filtering.** Option A: index every post with its audience class (public, friends-of-author, custom list) and have the shard intersect the term posting list with a filter derived from the viewer: public ∪ posts whose author is in friends(viewer). With ~hundreds of friends this is a union of author posting lists or a bitmap check, done inside the shard. Option B: ignore privacy in the index and post-filter, which is simple but wastes work when most matches are invisible (overfetch factor, empty pages). Do A for pruning, then always B as the safety net, because an index can lag a privacy change by seconds. Deletes and audience reductions are written first as tombstones/filters so they take effect even before the index catches up.
- **Freshness vs cost.** A small in-memory real-time segment accepts writes and is searched alongside large immutable segments; merging is background work. Edits are delete+insert. Under backlog, shed ranking work, never privacy checks.
- **Scatter-gather latency.** Fan-out multiplies tail latency: query only the time buckets needed (most queries want recent results), send hedged requests to replicas, return partial results at a deadline. Pre-compute friend sets in a cache per viewer.
- **Ranking.** Combine text match, recency decay and closeness (interaction counts with the author); cap candidates per shard before the expensive stage.
reference.wrapup:
- A time-partitioned inverted index fed by the post change stream, queried with scatter-gather and a viewer-based audience filter.
- Trade-offs: pre-filtering in the index vs post-filtering, index freshness vs write amplification, recall (older buckets) vs latency.
- Next: typo tolerance, hashtags and entity search, group posts, per-language analyzers, sub-second indexing.

rubric.text: Estimates post rate, index size from postings per post, and query QPS; notes the write-heavy index maintenance
Builds an inverted index (term to sorted posting lists) with tokenisation/normalisation
Feeds the index asynchronously from the post change stream (create, edit, delete, audience change)
Partitions the index by time bucket and/or document id hash; scatter-gather across shards with a coordinator merge
Enforces privacy inside the query by intersecting with an audience/friends filter
Re-checks permissions against the authoritative store at serve time because the index can be stale
Real-time segment plus immutable merged segments to get seconds-level freshness
Ranking by text relevance, recency and social closeness, with stable cursor pagination
Controls tail latency: hedged requests, deadlines/partial results, limit queried time ranges
Handles deletes and edits (tombstones, delete+insert) and index replication/recovery
Uses a time-ordered document id so recent postings are contiguous and cheap to skip
